## The re-proof verdict (the critical-path answer)

**Both repairs hold under real load.** The mediated-egress repair's live
verification stands (Wc2) and recurs cleanly (Wc3: no scope-mint violation,
no zero-decision signature); the `pkill`-free `terminate_group` repair is
now verified live — **zero** `cell-terminate` machinery exceptions on the
9 fully-surfaced members where Wc2 carried 3 verbatim `pkill`-absent
exceptions, and none of the ~900 s terminate stalls reappeared.

The covering verdicts did **not** land: the held leg ran to the 5 h dead-man
at **28/30 surfaces** — 3 surfaces short of the held packet. The pace is
honest real-work: O `3/3` on all 10 members, H-pub `3/3` on all 9 completed,
H-allow `0/3` on all 9 (`exited{0}` → `verifier_unavailable:reward_missing`,
the honest non-covering class). No `hh-reproof-packet/1` or register was
minted, `task_lists.state` stays **`blocked`** — honest, never rescued.

The window's own residual signals, recorded never excluded: (a) even D = 5 h
does not bound the held leg's real-trial pace at R=3 (two ~1 h+ slow-member
stretches — pypi-server H-allow ~1 h, query-optimize mid-flight at cutoff);
a split-leg (held→packet, dev→packet as separate windows) or a yet-longer-D
scope decision belongs to a later gate; (b) the driver poll deadline was
minted 5 h past intent (epoch computed in the controller's local TZ despite
the `Z` suffix — 15:30:45Z instead of 10:30:45Z); the in-guest dead-man is
the physical bound so the defect cost only operator-time at cutoff —
recorded verbatim.
